title: responses-vx-client-attribute-preserve-and-stream-stabilizer
author: Lena Ortiz
description: Motivation: Recent Responses API variants require stricter preservation of client-provided attributes (rng seeds, client metadata tags) and more robust streaming reassembly semantics when chunks are delivered out-of-order or partial. This PR implements a conservative stream-stabilizer state machine in the OpenAI-compat adapter, preserves and forwards client attribute headers into Responses vX framing, and tightens tool/function-call boundary markers to avoid misattribution during streaming reassembly. Goals: 1) Ensure rng/seed hints and opaque client metadata are present on the final assembled Response object and on any tool-call events emitted during streaming. 2) Make streaming tolerant to chunk loss and reordering by introducing sequence markers and a fallback reassembly path that requests a non-streaming re-fetch for the last-incomplete span. 3) Keep the compatibility layer backwards-compatible with existing vX-1 and vX behaviors; expose a toggle (compat.mode=stable-stream) for customers to opt into the stricter reassembly semantics. Summary of changes: - OpenAI adapter: add attributes header passthrough (x-rw-client-attrs/x-rw-rng-hint) and carry-through logic into response attributes. - Streaming reassembly: introduce StreamStabilizer with sequence markers, per-chunk checksum hint, and a compact reassembly buffer that triggers an inline re-fetch if a gap persists beyond a configurable window. - Tool/function call handling: emit explicit tool-call-start and tool-call-end markers in the chunk stream; attach preserved client attributes to tool-call events so downstream tooling receives the same metadata as final Responses objects. - SDKs: lightweight client header propagation helpers added to Python and TypeScript SDKs; example in examples/streams/toolcall-preserve.md. - Tests & CI: add deterministic replay tests for mixed-order chunk delivery and unit tests for attribute propagation. Backwards compatibility and rollout: default behavior remains conservative (existing flows unchanged). The new compat.mode flag is off by default; feature rollout to hosted begins with Canary and Dedicated beta. See release_notes field for user-facing changes and migration guidance.

release_notes: Feature: OpenAI-compat: stable-stream mode (opt-in) preserves client attributes (x-rw-client-attrs, x-rw-rng-hint) across streaming reassembly and tool-call events. Streaming is more robust to out-of-order/partial chunks via sequence markers and an inline re-fetch fallback. Impact: Default behavior unchanged. Dedicated/private customers can toggle compat.stable_stream.* settings to control reassembly window and buffer sizes. Migration: If you currently rely on implicit metadata inference from chunk payloads, switch to sending attributes in the x-rw-client-attrs header for stable behavior.
notes_for_ops: Canary rollout: enable compat.mode=stable-stream in canary region only; monitor rw.stream.gaps_detected and rw.stream.reassembly_fallbacks
Dedicated: add compat.stable_stream.window_ms to Dedicated UI and operator config; default 250ms, min 50ms
